title: Rapid Intravenous In Ovo Injection of Developing Amniote Embryos
author: Cooper, Santos-Durán, et al.
materials: Hamilton syringe with luer tip, 50 μL
Hamilton syringe, 700 series, with removable needles
Timing: Approximately 5 to 10 min per embryo

steps.title: Candle eggs to locate vein
steps.instruction: Identify a suitable chorioallantoic vein on each egg before injection.

substeps.instruction: Remove eggs from the incubator, keeping the upward‑facing side oriented as before.
Place each egg in a paraffin egg mount that is covered with damp tissue paper.
Wipe the upper surface of the egg gently with 70% ethanol.
In a dark room, illuminate the egg with a candling torch to visualize the chorioallantoic veins; move the torch around to locate the largest vein.
Draw a triangular window around the selected vein with a pencil; the window should be approximately 6 × 6 × 6 mm.
Repeat the procedure for all eggs, then return the eggs to the incubator until the next step.
Timing: approximately 2 min per egg.

steps.title: Cut window and apply mineral oil
steps.instruction: Create a shell window over the drawn area and increase membrane transparency with mineral oil.

substeps.instruction: Remove an egg from the incubator and position it in the paraffin mount.

Using a detailing saw, carefully cut through the eggshell within the penciled triangle, watching for a sudden change in texture that indicates the underlying membrane (the membrane appears whiter and rougher).
CRITICAL: Do not damage the membrane; piercings can let air bubbles in and dislodge veins.
Remove the cut shell fragment with fine forceps, exposing the membrane.
Repeat for all eggs.
With a cotton bud, apply a small amount of mineral oil to the exposed membrane to improve transparency; use more oil and rub persistently for reptilian eggs with thicker membranes.
Timing: approximately 4 min per egg.

steps.title: Inject drug into chorioallantoic vein
steps.instruction: Deliver the chosen solution directly into the vein through the windowed membrane.

substeps.instruction: Place the windowed egg on the paraffin mount on the stage of a dissecting microscope; keep damp tissue paper on the mount for stability.
Hold the candling torch against the side of the egg to illuminate the selected vein; re‑apply mineral oil if the vein is not sufficiently clear.

Load a syringe with the drug solution, ensuring no air bubbles are present. Use a long, flexible Hamilton needle (e.g., 32 G) for chicken eggs; for crocodile or tortoise eggs, use a shorter, less flexible hypodermic needle as listed in the key resources table.
For chicken embryos (E10 onward) inject 30 µL; for crocodile or tortoise embryos inject 30–50 µL. Include patent blue dye if desired for visual confirmation.
Using the micromanipulator, position the needle directly above the vein at an angle of ~45°, then advance the needle to penetrate the vein without exiting the lower surface.
Deliver the required volume, then gently retract the needle with the micromanipulator.
Wipe the area around the window with 70% ethanol to remove excess oil.
Cover the window and exposed membrane with clear adhesive tape, label the egg with a pencil, and return it to the incubator.
If incubating chicken embryos to hatching, turn off the incubator’s rocking function from E18 onward and maintain humidity.
Timing: approximately 5–10 min per egg.

steps.title: Dissect embryo and fix tissue
steps.instruction: Harvest the embryo, optionally label proliferating cells, and fix for downstream analysis.

substeps.instruction: Remove the egg from the incubator and peel off the adhesive tape.
If EdU labeling is required, inject through the original window (or an enlarged window made with fine scissors):
• Chicken embryos: inject 150 µL of 10 mg/mL EdU, incubate 2 h before fixation.
• Crocodile/tortoise embryos: inject 200 µL of 10 mg/mL EdU, incubate 3 h before fixation.
Enlarge the window if necessary with fine scissors, then cut the top of the egg starting from the window using small scissors.
Carefully extract the embryo with a blunt instrument (e.g., metal spoon) and place it in a dish of PBS at room temperature.
Decapitate the embryo immediately; for hatched animals, euthanize according to local regulations (e.g., sodium pentobarbital injection).
Dissect the tissue of interest, rinse briefly in fresh PBS, and transfer to fixative if fixation is required.
Fixation options:
• Overnight in 4 % paraformaldehyde in PBS followed by graded ethanol dehydration, or
• Store in 10 % neutral‑buffered formalin for long‑term preservation.
Timing: approximately 5–10 min per embryo.
